extracted.intended_audience: poets, fiction and creative nonfiction writers (authors seeking literary magazines and small presses open to submissions)
extracted.subtask_description: Locate literary magazines and small presses currently accepting submissions (with reading period dates and year‑round open lists) and use editorial policies and submission guidelines to determine fit and prepare submissions. The page is a continually updated directory of venues and procedural tips for submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit only during listed reading periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Each publication lists specific open dates (e.g., 'Feb 1 to Jun 15'); submit while the journal or press is 'open for submissions.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists exact start and end dates for reading periods for each magazine/press; check those dates and submit within them. Many publications have multiple windows per year (e.g., 'Apr 1 to Jun 30, Oct 1 to Dec 31').

rubrics_metrics.name: Match your submission to accepted genres
rubrics_metrics.description: Venues specify what they accept (e.g., 'Poetry, Fiction, Creative Nonfiction, Translation'); only submit work in genres the publication lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the genre tags shown next to each title to determine fit (poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction, translation, etc.). Choosing venues that 'share your vision for your work' increases fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult editorial policies and submission guidelines before submitting
rubrics_metrics.description: Research each publication’s editorial policies and submission guidelines—Poets & Writers notes the Literary Magazines database contains 'editorial policies, submission guidelines, contact information—everything you need to know before submitting your work.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read a venue’s submission guidelines for formatting, simultaneous-submission policy, fees (if any), length limits, cover-letter expectations, and rights/licensing terms; failure to follow guidelines can disqualify a submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use vetted/curated resources to find legitimate venues
rubrics_metrics.description: Poets & Writers curates and vets the publications and contests they list, stating they 'carefully review the practices and policies of each contest before including it' in their databases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize listings from vetted directories (like Poets & Writers databases) to avoid predatory or illegitimate contests and publishers; look for editorial staff info and transparent policies as signs of legitimacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check and recheck venue status because listings are updated continually
rubrics_metrics.description: The list is 'continually updated, so check back often.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before preparing/submitting work, verify the current status on the venue’s own site—reading periods and policies can change; do not rely solely on cached or old directory data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use organizational tools to track submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Poets & Writers recommends using their 'Submission Tracker to help you stay organized and keep track of your submissions.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep records of where and when you submitted, response/rejection dates, simultaneous submissions, and any rights agreements; this reduces accidental simultaneous submissions and missed response windows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify year‑round open venues separately
rubrics_metrics.description: The page includes a separate 'Open All Year' list for publications that accept submissions any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need flexibility, consult the 'Open All Year' list—but still read each publication’s guidelines and check for any rolling-response timelines or backlog notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find venues that align with your work and career goals
rubrics_metrics.description: The site advises: 'Find a home for your poems, stories, essays, and reviews by researching the publications vetted by our editorial staff' and to 'find a place to submit your work' among titles that 'share your vision for your work.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider editorial slant, audience, prestige, and the publisher’s distribution/visibility when choosing where to submit—not just whether they are open. Use the Literary Magazines and Small Presses databases to assess fit and potential career impact.
